basis: Cerebellar and autonomic neurodegeneration; bladder, swallowing and breathing abnormalities reflect neural dysfunction rather than direct visceral injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: stridor and central apnea reflect neural dysfunction; direct airway or lung injury is not established.
decisions.renal: none: frequent neurogenic bladder dysfunction reflects autonomic degeneration rather than direct urinary tract injury.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: neuromuscular dysphagia and constipation reflect neural dysfunction without established direct gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Epithelioid sarcoma commonly originates in dermal/subcutaneous and tendon-associated connective tissues; childhood specifies age rather than another site.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: dermis and subcutis are characteristic sites of origin of conventional childhood epithelioid sarcoma.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic deficiency; developmental impairment, dystonia and callosal malformation in 1/1; hip dysplasia in 1/1. Adrenal insufficiency shares the endocrine axis.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment, dystonia and callosal malformation occur in 1/1; the defining disorder is oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.

basis: SCID defined by profound T-cell deficiency, documented in 11/11; this affects an immune blood-cell lineage. Site-specific infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: absent or profoundly decreased T lymphocytes define the disease, establishing a blood-cell disorder as well as immunodeficiency.

basis: Autoinflammatory recurrent peritoneal/pleural serositis defines FMF. Joint attacks usually resolve without damage; persistent destructive arthritis is <30%. Renal amyloidosis is separate.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent pleural serositis is a defining manifestation; pleuritis is frequent (30-79%) in the supplied HPO data.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: arthralgia and acute arthritis usually resolve without residual injury; persistent destructive arthritis affects fewer than 30%.

basis: Adrenal cortisol excess causes muscle/bone loss and dermal atrophy/striae, each in roughly 50-80%. Hypertension is a separately diagnosed associated disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension occurs in roughly 70-80%, but is separately diagnosed; common direct cardiac or vascular structural damage is not established.

basis: Intestinal hamartomas, lipomas/lentiginosis and vascular malformations characterize BRRS; scoliosis/pectus deformity occurs in 30-79%. Neurologic impairment is occasional.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangiomas and vascular malformations are characteristic defining lesions, supported by vascular ancestry and HPO frequencies of 80-99%.

basis: Adrenal steroid synthesis disorder explicitly defined by mineralocorticoid-mediated hypertension (80-99%). Accelerated skeletal maturation alone does not establish bone damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertension is explicitly part of the definition and identifies the hypertensive CAH form; supplied frequency is 80-99%.

basis: GPI-anchor disorder with developmental disability; skeletal defects and cataracts each 2/2. Lung disease 1/2 omitted at cap; renal echogenicity alone does not prove dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: osteopenia, hip dysplasia, shortened distal phalanges and contractures occur in 2/2, supporting skeletal damage accompanying the metabolic/neurodevelopmental syndrome.

basis: Immune attack with diagnostic skin and oral lesions; ocular sicca/corneal injury occurs in 30-79%. Frequent hepatic and pulmonary involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic oral mucosal lesions are diagnostic manifestations; mouth and salivary glands belong to this axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic lichenoid and sclerotic skin lesions are diagnostic manifestations; skin thickening is reported in 80-99%.
